beats.title: Intro: The Burger Problem
beats.says: Two burgers and a fries cost £11. One burger and a fries cost £7. How much is a burger? Look at the difference between the two orders: it's just one burger, and the price goes up by £4. So a burger costs £4. That's simultaneous equations, and you just solved one.

beats.title: The Picture: Lots of Answers
beats.says: Now with letters: x for a burger, y for the fries. On its own, x plus y equals 7 has loads of answers: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4, and more. Plot them all, and they make a straight line.

beats.title: The Picture: Where They Cross
beats.says: Now plot the other equation, 2x plus y equals 11. It's a different line. There's only one point that sits on both lines: where they cross, at 4 and 3. That's the answer: a burger is £4 and the fries are £3.
beats.key: The answer is where the two lines cross: it works in both equations.

beats.title: The Method: Elimination
beats.says: In the exam you don't draw graphs. You use elimination. Line the equations up. Both have exactly one y, so subtract the bottom from the top. The y's cancel, leaving x equals 4.
beats.key: Same letter, same amount, same sign? Subtract to cancel it.

beats.title: The Method: Substitute Back
beats.says: Now put x equals 4 back into either equation. 4 plus y equals 7, so y is 3. Then check it in the other one: 2 times 4, plus 3, is 11. It works.
beats.onScreen: Worked: 4 + y = 7 // put x = 4 back in | y = 3 | check: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11 ✓ // always check in the other one
beats.key: Substitute back to find the other letter, then check.

beats.title: Making Them Match: Multiply First
beats.says: Usually nothing matches straight away. 3x plus 2y equals 16, and x plus y equals 6. Multiply the bottom equation by 2, so both have 2y. Now subtract. The y's cancel, leaving x equals 4. Then 4 plus y equals 6, so y is 2.
beats.key: Nothing matches? Multiply one equation so a letter does.

beats.title: Different Signs: Add
beats.says: If the signs are different, add instead. 2x plus y equals 9, and 3x minus y equals 11. Add them: plus y and minus y cancel, leaving 5x equals 20. So x is 4, and y is 1.
beats.key: Same signs subtract, different signs add.

beats.title: Substitution: When y = …
beats.says: If one equation already says y equals something, swap it straight in. y equals 2x plus 1, and 3x plus y equals 16. Replace y with 2x plus 1. That gives 5x plus 1 equals 16, so x is 3. Then y is 2 times 3, plus 1, which is 7.
beats.key: One equation says y = …? Substitute it in.

beats.title: Exam Tips: Common Mistakes
beats.says: The mistakes that lose marks: subtracting when the signs are different, slipping up with negatives, stopping after the first letter, and not checking your answer in both equations.
beats.onScreen: Worked: ✗ subtracting +y and −y // different signs: add | ✗ 11 − (−3) = 8 // minus a negative is plus: 14 | ✗ x = 4, then stop // find y too | ✓ match · cancel · solve · substitute · check

beats.title: Your Turn: Question
beats.says: Your turn. Solve x plus y equals 10, and x minus y equals 4. Pause the video and try it.
beats.onScreen: Your turn: question card with a countdown. Q: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 4.
beats.question: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 4

beats.title: Your Turn: Answer
beats.says: The signs on the y's are different, so add: 2x equals 14, so x is 7. Then 7 plus y equals 10, so y is 3. If you got that, you've got it.
beats.onScreen: Your turn: the answer A: x = 7, y = 3.
